findings.issue_category: public bucket access / no ACL restriction
findings.description: The bucket is explicitly commented as public and has no acl attribute set to private, nor any public access block or bucket policy restricting access, allowing anonymous or unauthorized access to potentially sensitive data (contains customer-master.xlsx).
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.

No versioning block is configured, meaning accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (e.g., the customer master file) cannot be recovered, increasing the impact of the public exposure noted above.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in publicly accessible unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A customer master data file is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing potentially sensitive customer information to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored operational data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so objects in the data-science bucket are stored unencrypted at rest despite having versioning and logging enabled.
